title: Phase I trial combining sulfasalazine and gamma knife radiosurgery for recurrent glioblastoma☆
author: Skeie, Sleire, et al.

steps.title: Baseline imaging acquisition
steps.instruction: Before the first sulfasalazine dose, obtain a baseline MRI, a [¹¹C]methionine PET, and a GSH‑edited MRS on a 3 T Siemens Biograph mMR (VE11P) using a head/neck matrix coil (12/20 channels). For MRS, use a MEGA‑PRESS sequence (TR = 2000 ms, TE = 80 ms) with 256 transients alternating edit‑ON/off, spectral width 4000 Hz, 4096 data points, 15 ms editing pulses at 4.56 ppm (ON) and 7.5 ppm (OFF), CHESS water suppression, and shimming with 3D‑DESS (or FASTESTMAP). Place a 27 mL voxel (30 × 30 × 30 mm³) in the tumor (maximizing coverage of contrast‑enhancing tissue while avoiding ventricles) and a second 27 mL voxel in the midline anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) as a healthy reference, adjusting as needed. Analyze spectra with Gannet 3.3.2, disabling spectral alignment, and report water‑referenced GSH concentrations without tissue‑content correction. Record quality metrics (e.g., SNR GSH median 8.05 [3.03‑12.9] healthy, 4.16 [2.25‑8.83] lesion; FWHM GSH median 10.1 [5.46‑14.7] Hz healthy, 11.8 [5.15‑23.11] Hz lesion) and exclude data if FWHM > 30 Hz, SNR < 50 % of median, or any estimate > 3 × median absolute deviation from baseline healthy side.

steps.title: Sulfasalazine dosing schedule
steps.instruction: Administer oral sulfasalazine once daily. Give the first dose on Day 1, the second on Day 2, and the third dose on Day 3 at approximately 07:00.

steps.title: Day‑3 pre‑GKRS MRS
steps.instruction: At approximately 09:00 on Day 3 (after the third sulfasalazine dose and before GKRS), repeat the GSH‑edited MRS using the identical hardware, voxel locations, and sequence parameters described in the baseline step.

steps.title: Gamma Knife radiosurgery delivery
steps.instruction: Between 12:00 and 14:00 on Day 3, perform a single‑session Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) using a Leksell stereotactic frame and contrast‑enhanced stereotactic MRI (1‑mm slices) for target definition. Define the target as the contrast‑enhancing tumor volume on T1‑post‑contrast MRI with no additional margin. Prescribe a dose of 12 Gy to the 50 % isodose line (for lesions ≤1 cm³, use a prescription isodose line of 50‑90 %). Optimize the plan to achieve a conformity ratio ≈1.0 (acceptable range 0.75‑1.25), gradient index ≤3.0 (PCI < 90 %), and minimize the 12‑Gy volume outside the target (V₁₂Gy). Apply normal‑tissue constraints: brainstem V₁₂Gy < 1 mL, optic apparatus maximum dose < 8 Gy, cochlear maximum dose < 4 Gy, and total treated volume ≤15 cm³. Exclude patients with prior repeat fractionated re‑irradiation or GKRS at the same target.

substeps.instruction: Position patient in Leksell frame and acquire contrast‑enhanced stereotactic MRI.
Contour target (contrast‑enhancing tumor) on T1‑post‑contrast images.
Set prescription: 12 Gy to 50 % isodose (or 50‑90 % for ≤1 cm³ lesions).
Generate treatment plan, evaluate conformity, gradient, PCI, and V₁₂Gy metrics.
Verify normal‑tissue dose constraints and adjust plan as needed.
Deliver the treatment in a single session.

steps.title: Day‑4 post‑GKRS MRS
steps.instruction: Approximately 24 hours after GKRS (Day 4), repeat the GSH‑edited MRS using the same voxel placements and acquisition parameters as the baseline and Day‑3 scans.

steps.title: One‑month follow‑up imaging
steps.instruction: At the 1‑month visit, repeat MRI, optional [¹¹C]methionine PET, and GSH‑edited MRS using the identical protocols to assess contrast enhancement, tumor size, and glutathione dynamics.

steps.title: Long‑term MRI follow‑up
steps.instruction: Perform MRI (T1 with and without contrast, T2, and FLAIR) at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months post‑treatment. Repeat PET only if clinically indicated (e.g., suspected pseudoprogression).

steps.title: PET acquisition details
steps.instruction: For each PET scan, inject [¹¹C]methionine intravenously according to a weight‑based protocol, then wait a controlled uptake time of 10–20 minutes (¹¹C half‑life ≈ 20.3 min). Acquire PET on the integrated 3 T PET/MRI system, reconstruct with MR‑based attenuation correction and the OASIS pipeline. Place the lesion VOI on the region of highest methionine uptake while excluding necrotic or hemorrhagic tissue; place the reference VOI in contralateral normal‑appearing cortex or white matter. Extract SUVmax, SUVmean, and compute tumor‑to‑normal (T/N) ratios. Apply PET‑RANO 1.0 criteria for metabolic response.

steps.title: Data collection and management
steps.instruction: Record all imaging, dosing, and adverse‑event data in protocol‑specific case report forms (CRFs). Monitor CRFs regularly for completeness, consistency, and accuracy. De‑identify all datasets before analysis and store them in secure institutional repositories in compliance with local data‑protection regulations. An independent Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) and steering committee will oversee safety and protocol adherence.

steps.title: Statistical analysis plan
steps.instruction: Perform statistical analyses using validated software (SPSS and R). Primary endpoint: determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and recommended phase II dose (RP2D) of sulfasalazine as a radiosensitizer based on the number of participants experiencing CTCAE v4.0 grade ≥ 3 adverse events per dose cohort (no formal hypothesis testing). Secondary endpoints: summarize descriptively; analyze time‑to‑event outcomes (FFLP, PFS, OS) with Kaplan‑Meier curves and Cox models; analyze longitudinal outcomes (tumor volume, KPS, FACT‑Br, SUVmax, GSH levels) with mixed‑effects models for repeated measures, including fixed effects for time (and time × region for GSH/SUVmax), baseline score, age, sex, and random intercept and slope for each subject. Apply Šidák adjustment for pairwise time‑point contrasts.
